title: A second objection: 'Now I know that you fear God' (Genesis 22)
source_text: XI. Et certe Deum quiddam circa liberas hominum actiones de novo discere, plane confici videtur ipsius Dei verbis Abrahamum alloquentis, ejusdem libri capite vigesimo secundo. Postquam enim Abraham se paratum ostendisset ad filium, ex Dei mandato, immolandum; Nunc cognovi, inquit Dominus, quod timeas Deum, quia non pepercisti unigenito tuo filio propter me.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly that God learns something anew about the free actions of men, seems plainly to be concluded from the words of God himself addressing Abraham, in the twenty-second chapter of the same book. For after Abraham had shown himself ready to sacrifice his son, by the command of God; Now I know, says the Lord, that thou fearest God, because thou hast not spared thine only begotten son for my sake.
pass_b_english: And certainly it seems plainly to follow from God's own words to Abraham in Genesis 22 that he learns something new about the free actions of human beings.
After Abraham had shown himself ready to sacrifice his son at God's command, the Lord says: 'Now I know that you fear God, because you have not spared your only son for my sake.'

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
